title: Microsoft Purview Data Security Investigations: Admin and Contributor roles added to existing Purview role groups
summary: Hold: the page incorrectly says Security Administrator membership cannot be managed on the Purview Role groups page. Microsoft permits portal changes for security and compliance, while directing administrators to Entra for central management. The role additions, roadmap details and consumption billing are supported.

claims.claim: The Security Administrator role group inherits Entra Security Administrator membership, thereby conferring its DSI Contributor access.
claims.quote: the Security Administrator role from Microsoft Entra ID is assigned to this role group. Therefore, this role group inherits the capabilities and membership of the Security Administrator role from Microsoft Entra ID.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Microsoft directs administrators to manage Security Administrator membership centrally in the Microsoft Entra admin center.
claims.quote: To manage permissions centrally, add and remove group members in the Microsoft Entra admin center.

claims.claim: Security Administrator members are managed in Entra, not on the Purview Role groups page.
claims.quote: If you edit this role group in these portals (membership or roles), those changes apply only to the security and compliance areas and not to any other services.
claims.fix: Replace the sentence with: 'Manage Security Administrator membership centrally in the Microsoft Entra admin center. Editing this role group's membership or roles in the Purview portal affects only security and compliance, not other services.' Keep the citation to https://learn.microsoft.com/defender-office-365/scc-permissions.

claims.claim: Only DSI Admin-role holders can access the usage dashboard, including members of the groups that include that role.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls
claims.claim: Role group permission changes can take up to 30 minutes to apply.
claims.quote: After you configure your role groups, it might take up to 30 minutes for the role group permissions to apply to assigned users across your organization.

claims.claim: The documented general Purview portal steps for adding and removing members require an account assigned Role management.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal by using credentials for an admin account assigned the Role management role.

claims.claim: Microsoft advises keeping at least one member in Data Security Investigations Admins.
claims.quote: Always have at least one user in the Data Security Investigations Admins role group so that your Data Security Investigations configuration doesn't get in to a 'zero administrator' scenario if specific users leave your organization.

claims.claim: The Purview removal path is Settings > Roles and scopes > Role groups > Role groups for Microsoft Purview solutions > role group > Edit > Edit members of the role group > Remove members.
claims.quote: Go to Settings > Roles and scopes ... Select Role groups. ... On Role groups for Microsoft Purview solutions, select a Microsoft Purview role group ... Select Edit ... On Edit members of the role group ... Select Remove members

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls table; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Remove-RoleGroupMember -Identity "<role-group>" -Member "<user-UPN>" removes a member from the identified role group.
claims.quote: Remove-RoleGroupMember [-Identity] <RoleGroupIdParameter> -Member <SecurityPrincipalIdParameter> ... The Member parameter specifies who to remove from the role group. ... User ID or user principal name (UPN)

claims.claim: The cited DSI page gives Settings > Roles and groups > Role groups > Data Security Investigations Admins > Edit > Choose users.
claims.quote: select Roles and groups, then select Role groups in the left navigation. ... Select the Data Security Investigations Admins role group, then select Edit. ... Select Choose users
claims.fix: Append to controls[1].note: 'The DSI permissions page gives Roles and groups; the general Purview permissions page instead gives Settings > Roles and scopes > Role groups > Role groups for Microsoft Purview solutions > role group > Edit > Edit members of the role group > Choose users.' Both pages are already cited.

claims.claim: Add-RoleGroupMember -Identity "<role-group>" -Member "<user-UPN>" adds a user to the dedicated DSI administrator role group when that group is the target.
claims.quote: Add-RoleGroupMember [-Identity] <RoleGroupIdParameter> -Member <SecurityPrincipalIdParameter> ... When you add a member to a role group, the member is given the effective permissions provided by the management roles assigned to the role group.

claims.claim: The add-with-optional-expiry path stops at Settings > Roles and scopes > Role groups > Role groups for Microsoft Purview solutions > role group > Edit > Edit members of the role group > Choose users.
claims.quote: On Edit members of the role group, select Choose users or Choose groups. ... If the selected users or groups need temporary access, select the users or groups and select Edit expiration.
claims.fix: The printed steps reach the correct membership page but stop before the expiry control. Add to controls[2].note: 'To set expiry, select the users added on Edit members of the role group, then select Edit expiration.' Keep the existing add path.

claims.claim: Add-RoleGroupMember -Identity "<role-group>" -Member "<user-UPN>" adds the identified user; the note does not claim it sets expiry.
claims.quote: The Identity parameter specifies the role group to add a member to. ... The Member parameter specifies who you want to add to the role group. ... User ID or user principal name (UPN)

claims.claim: Edit expiration provides temporary Purview role group access, including for DSI role groups.
claims.quote: All built-in and custom role groups except the following support automatic expiring permissions: eDiscovery Administrator eDiscovery Manager

claims.claim: The Add-RoleGroupMember syntax lists no expiration parameter.
claims.quote: Searched: Add-RoleGroupMember expiration parameter Security Compliance PowerShell; opened Add-RoleGroupMember reference. Its full syntax lists Identity, Member, BypassSecurityGroupManagerCheck, Confirm, DomainController, WhatIf and CommonParameters, with no expiration parameter.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Get-RoleGroupMember -Identity <role group> retrieves a role group's members.
claims.quote: Use the Get-RoleGroupMember cmdlet to retrieve a list of members of a management role group. ... The Identity parameter specifies the role group for which member information should be retrieved.

claims.claim: Purview role groups are shared across compliance and governance solutions rather than confined to DSI.
claims.quote: A role group is a set of roles that enable users to do their jobs across compliance and governance solutions in the Microsoft Purview portal.

claims.claim: Removing a role group member removes access to its features where that group was the member's only access route.
claims.quote: When you remove a member from a role group, that member can no longer manage the features made available by the role group if the role group is the only means by which the member is granted access to the feature.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model and notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: DSI uses consumption billing based on storage and AI compute, not a dedicated enterprise plan or licence.
claims.quote: Billing in Data Security Investigations is based solely on the combination of the amount of stored data and the associated computing capacity needed for AI analysis. It isn't based on a dedicated enterprise plan or license.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Licence; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Microsoft publishes no licence specific to the role change.
claims.quote: Searched: DSI role based access simplification 558546 license charge role change; DSI role license billing simplification (DSI expanded in queries). Read DSI billing, permissions, overview and Purview permissions; no role-change-specific licence found.

claims.claim: Microsoft publishes no charge specific to the role change.
claims.quote: Searched: DSI role based access simplification 558546 license charge role change; DSI role license billing simplification (DSI expanded in queries). Read DSI billing and overview; no charge specifically for the role change found.

claims.claim: DSI collects organisational content into investigations.
claims.quote: The investigation helps you analyze the alert details, understand what they mean, and collect and examine data for deeper review and mitigation efforts.
claims.fix: Add 'Learn about Data Security Investigations', https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/data-security-investigations, to sources to support the content-collection statement.

claims.where: Why it matters; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: DSI performs AI analysis on investigation data.
claims.quote: Data Security Investigations Compute Units (compute unit) measure the computational capacity needed to run the AI analysis within Data Security Investigations.

claims.claim: The pay-as-you-go storage meter charges per GB per month for investigation data.
claims.quote: The storage meter for Data Security Investigations uses the pay-as-you-go billing model. You pay for storage on a gigabyte (GB) per month basis for stored data associated with all investigations in your organization.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Meters; rationale: cost
claims.claim: AI analysis is billed for Data Security Investigations Compute Units used.
claims.quote: Data Security Investigations uses the pay-as-you-go billing model for AI capacity. You need compute units for deep analysis and AI-related processing in your investigations. You pay only for the compute units you use.

claims.claim: Storage billing is linked to an Azure subscription during setup.
claims.quote: Storage meter billing requires a link to an Azure subscription for pay-as-you-go billing. ... Azure subscription: The Azure subscription you want to assign to the storage meter.

claims.claim: The Azure subscription must be in the same tenant as Microsoft Purview.
claims.quote: To configure the storage meter and capacity for Data Security Investigations, you must have: An Azure subscription in the same tenant as Microsoft Purview.

claims.where: Scope: Prerequisite for any metered use
claims.claim: DSI billing must be configured before metered use.
claims.quote: Before you can use Data Security Investigations in your organization, you must configure both billing models.

claims.claim: Microsoft points readers to the Azure Microsoft Purview pricing page for storage rates.
claims.quote: For more data storage rates and pricing, see Data Security Investigations storage meter pricing. [https://azure.microsoft.com/pricing/details/purview/]

claims.claim: Deleting an investigation stops its associated storage charge.
claims.quote: When you delete an investigation, you stop paying for the associated data storage amount.

claims.claim: Storage charges are prorated by the days the data was stored.
claims.quote: The charges are prorated to the number of days the data was stored in the billing cycle.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Spend controls; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft recommends Azure budgets at the DSI resource group and meter level with spending-threshold alerts.
claims.quote: Create budgets for the Data Security Investigations resource group and meter level. Configure alerts when spending approaches defined thresholds

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Spend controls; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: The DSI usage dashboard tracks storage and compute usage for individual investigations.
claims.quote: Use the Pay-as-you-go usage dashboard to quickly view and track data storage and compute unit usage for each investigation in your organization.

claims.claim: Azure budgets and alerts are not a consumption cap.
claims.quote: Notifications are triggered when the budget thresholds are exceeded. Resources aren't affected, and your consumption isn't stopped.
claims.fix: Cite 'Tutorial: Create and manage budgets', https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/cost-management-billing/costs/tutorial-acm-create-budgets, for the statement that Azure budgets do not stop consumption.

claims.claim: The usage dashboard is a tracking surface rather than a spending cap.
claims.quote: Use the Pay-as-you-go usage dashboard to quickly view and track data storage and compute unit usage for each investigation in your organization. ... The current data storage and compute unit totals for each investigation help you manage usage and cost per investigation.

claims.claim: The role-assignment change adds no new automated action beyond granting access to existing DSI functions.
claims.quote: Searched: Data Security Investigations role-based access automation action; role based access simplification 558546. Read roadmap, DSI permissions and overview. No new automated action documented for the role additions.

claims.claim: The checklist names controls absent from the controls table.
claims.quote: Checklist: Get-RoleGroupMember inventory; Entra Security Administrator review; DSI usage dashboard review; Azure budget alerts. Table: removal, dedicated DSI admin membership, adding members with optional expiry.
claims.fix: The membership-inventory, Entra Security Administrator, DSI usage-dashboard and Azure-budget checklist steps have no corresponding control rows. Remove these four checklist instructions, and the repeated Entra membership re-check instruction under After rollout; retain the supported explanatory prose. Do not add control rows as part of this correction.
